newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kodak welcomes WTO panel on film row with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Kodak welcomes WTO panel on film row with Japan.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Company on Wednesday welcomed the setting up of a dispute settlement panel by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to look into the "anticompetitive trade practices" it said were backed by Japan.
In a statement distributed by Kodak officials at WTO headquarters, the U.S. photofilm giant also defended the U.S. domestic market as being "the most open market in the world".

The neutral panel was formally established by the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body to look into a U.S. complaint that Japan rigs its photofilm market to protect domestic giant Fuji from foreign competition, officials said. The European Union joined the dispute as a third party, they added.
"Today's action signifies the beginning of the WTO's formal investigation into anti-competitive trade practices supported by the Government of Japan," the Kodak statement said.

Kodak, which is based in Rochester, New York, said the WTO panel would examine evidence detailing "the many laws and measures" established by Japan "which restrict foreign access to Japan's market for photographic products".
Kodak said that these laws contravened Japan's obligations under the rules of the 123-member trade watchdog.

"Japan has refused to discuss the case for more than a year. With the establishment of this panel at the WTO, there is an informed and effective mechanism to evaluate the wealth of evidence which supports the U.S. government's case," Daniel Carp, Kodak's assistant chief operating officer, was quoted as saying.
"It is unfortunate...that the Government of Japan continues in its attempts to evade the issues," he added.
Japan's government denies the U.S. charges and has called for parallel consultations on alleged anti-competitive practices in the American photofilm market.

Kodak's Carp said: "Suggestions for an investigation into the U.S. market is clearly a diversionary tactic. The U.S. market is the most open in the world. Fuji's recent agreements with several U.S. retailers are ample proof of this fact."
Kodak and Fuji, the two world rivals, dominate global sales of photofilm and paper, with Kodak holding 36 per cent and Fuji 33 per cent.
Fuji holds around 67 per cent of the Japanese market for photofilm and paper while Kodak has 70 per cent of the U.S. domestic market but only between seven and 10 per cent in Japan.
Kodak officials have claimed Fuji's dominance has caused it to lose business worth $5.6 billion over the last decade.
Kodak also said it expected the WTO panel to issue its preliminary findings within six months.

Washington will also pursue Japan's violation of the General Agreement on Trade and Services (GATS) and is seeking consultations with Japan under WTO procedures so as to address "exclusionary business practices which exist in the Japanese market", according to the Kodak statement.
